A large sample of synthetic catchments

Source: R/synthetic_basins.R
synthetic_basins.Rd

Writes n synthetic catchments as basin folders that calibrate_batch() reads directly, each with its own climate and its own true model. Calibrating the whole sample then shows, across many catchments at once, what automatic calibration recovers, because every truth is known.

Usage

synthetic_basins(
  folder,
  n = 30,
  years = 10,
  dt = 24,
  start = "2010-10-01",
  seed = 1,
  ranges = list()
)

Arguments

folder

Folder to write the basin folders into; created if needed. Existing basin folders of the same names are refused.

n

Number of catchments.

years, dt, start

Length (years), step (hours) and first time of every record.

seed

Seed for the whole sample; each catchment is reproducible from it.

ranges

Named list of c(low, high) ranges for area_km2, wetness, storminess, pet_mean (mm/day), fc, cmax (mm), b, kg (h), k1 (h) and kb. Names left out keep their defaults.

Value

The sample, invisibly: a data frame with one row per basin giving its climate (mean annual rain and PET, mm), its true parameters, its mean flow and its highest gauged flow. It is also written to sample.csv in folder. Each basin folder holds forcing.csv, flow.csv, basin.yml and truth.yml, the true configuration.

Details

Climate. Each catchment's rain comes from the Neyman-Scott generator (synthetic_rain()) with the built-in parameters changed in two ways: wetness scales the cell intensity, and so the annual total; storminess multiplies the number of cells per storm and divides their intensity by the same factor, so storms grow more clustered and intense with no change in the total. Potential evaporation has its own annual mean.

Catchment. The true model is the standard structure. Its area and parameters are drawn independently for each catchment: uniformly for fc and b, and uniformly on a log scale for the area and for the parameters that span orders of magnitude. The second surface store is the first times a factor between 1 and 3. Every drawn value lies inside calibration_bounds(). The ranges are arguments, so a sample can be made of any kind of catchment.

Gauge. Each catchment is recorded with persistent gauge error and, above the flow exceeded 0.5 per cent of the time, a rating 15 per cent low at twice that flow, as synthetic_catchment() describes. The highest gauged flow goes into basin.yml, so registration flags the flows above it.

Windows. After a warm-up of three months, the first 70 per cent of the record is for calibration and the rest for validation. With seven years or more, the batch holds back each record's two wettest years; shorter records hold back none (wettest_years: 0).

See also

synthetic_catchment(), calibrate_batch()

Examples

# \donttest{
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "sample")
sample <- synthetic_basins(folder, n = 3, years = 4, seed = 1)
sample[, c("basin", "area_km2", "rain_mm", "cmax", "kg")]
#>   basin  area_km2   rain_mm     cmax       kg
#> 1  S001 363.44064  614.8391 451.5064  603.834
#> 2  S002  50.97558 1127.0547 427.3862 1763.074
#> 3  S003 201.46167  504.1416 515.9590 1029.217
unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
# }
